answer.rationale: The competitor price cut creates strong pull toward promotional_pricing, but memory_73 is explicit and unusually specific: promotional pricing lifted acquisition and revenue while materially reducing 30-day retention, with a standing instruction not to generalize it. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, matching a price cut would buy short-term account preservation while degrading exactly the metric that defines the objective; urgency is not evidence, and today's churn conversations do not overturn that recorded caveat. Of the remaining options, two are backed by source records I independently recovered this cycle: exp_86 (onboarding: completion +13%, TTV -2.1 days, retention +3%) and exp_91 (activation messaging: week-one engagement +11%, activation +6%, retention +1%). Both are confirmed rather than merely consolidated. I choose activation_messaging because the acute problem is retention pressure on existing SMB accounts, and in-product messaging is the only verified lever that reaches accounts already in the product and works by increasing realized value — the durable defense against a price-based attack, since accounts that have reached meaningful use are less substitutable on price alone. simplify_onboarding is equally well verified but acts on the top of the funnel and cannot help accounts already at risk. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is real but addresses a different segment than the one under attack. referral_incentive (memory_57) presumes goodwill in a base currently in churn conversations and could surface poorly. Key uncertainty I am not resolving away: exp_91's evidence is for week-one, newly activated accounts; extending it to tenured, price-sensitive accounts weighing a competitor offer is an extrapolation, not a demonstrated result. That gap is why I run a standard experiment with a holdout rather than a broad rollout — a broad push would spend the one verified lever I have on an untested population and leave no clean read. Downstream risk flagged: if leadership reads this as a substitute for pricing strategy, the unverified inference that value messaging neutralizes a structural price gap will harden into assumed fact and propagate into next quarter's planning. It should be logged as a hypothesis under test. Next cycle, when budget returns, memory_73 is the first priority to re-verify — it is the memory most likely to be pressured into a rollout, and its retention caveat is currently unconfirmed by any source record I hold; memory_31, memory_57, and memory_44 remain consolidated-only and should follow.
